newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares stable in institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares stable in institutional buying.

text.p: Jordan shares on Tuesday were underpinned by local institutional buying on blue-chips and firms expected to post healthy half year earnings, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.04 percent to 164.03 points in turnover worth 957,283 dinars ($1,4 million).
Brokers said prices were underpinned by local portfolio buying on leading industrial and services firms which are forecast or have already announced healthy first half earnings.

"There was nothing exceptional in today's trade and prices were within their ranges, but there was institutional buying along with selling by individual investors in need of cash," said Nasser al-Amad, general manager of United Financial Investments.
Jordan Cement Factory, which has been a focus of foreign fund interest over the last few months, rose 0.02 dinars to 3.99 dinars in the day's largest volume, worth 269,722 dinars.
Amad said foreign investor interest was currently subdued as global funds await half-year performance of popular blue-chips.
Some firms have already announced their results but many still have not, with a mixed outlook so far compared to the same period last year, he said.
Investor interest was maintained in Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, which remained unchanged at 4.15 dinars in trade worth 34,140 dinars.
Jordan Electric Power rose 0.02 to 1.69 dinars in healthy 68,543 dinars worth of trade.

Brokers said the renewed interest in the firm was sparked by prospects of further privatisation moves in the power sector after last week's announcement by the government of its plans to sell a 50 percent stake in Irbid Electricity.
Overall 16 shares rose and 12 fell, with another 20 trading but closing unchanged.
